done_when: forge merge enable changes an existing merge key wherever and however forge.toml writes it (indented, single- or double-quoted, with a comment) and adds one only when there is none, and the file still parses; a test covers each form

findings.body: The regex selects the first line that looks like a merge assignment, even if it is content inside a multiline string. For example, a valid forge.toml can contain `test = """\nmerge = "human"\n"""` before a real top-level `merge = "human"`. The substitution changes the test string, leaves the actual merge key unchanged, and then refuses the command. `test` is an accepted string setting in `src/forge/repo.py:132` and its validation at line 281 permits multiline strings. Locate the actual TOML key before editing it. This is a different case from the previously ruled table-looking line: the new matcher itself now selects the line inside the string.
findings.title: Handle merge-looking lines inside multiline TOML strings

why: forge merge enable adds a second merge key when forge.toml writes it indented or quoted, which breaks the file
